answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring each identity to post a refundable bond and build a verifiable thread of completed, peer-reviewed work before it can vote or take large jobs. Newcomers start in a shallow lagoon of low-trust tasks, earning reputation only through consistent, checkable performance. That history is a costly signal: one credible identity takes weeks of real work and locked funds, so faking a thousand votes means funding and working a thousand identities.
